headline: Milford holds Freightways as a core position across multiple funds, backed by NZ cyclical recovery, Australian expansion and acquisition track record.
reasoning: Milford's investment case rests on three pillars: a return to growth in the New Zealand Express Package segment driven by local economic recovery, same-customer volume growth and market share gains; a large Australian growth story following the Adelaide Express acquisition with strong organic volume growth and scope for further geographic expansion; and value creation through further acquisitions given management's strong track record. Despite a short-term blip from the Iran energy shock in 2026, the share price recovered and the medium-term thesis remains intact. Freightways consistently delivers returns above cost of capital and has strongly aligned management, making it a core holding across several Milford funds.
quote: Our investment case in freightways is based on a few factors. Firstly, a return to attractive growth in the New Zealand express package segment. This is helped by local cyclical economic recovery and there has been strong evidence of this through same customer volume growth. and also there has been some market share gains in New Zealand which is the cream on top. Secondly, there is a large Australian growth story. Since the acquisition of Adelide Express, there has been some impressive organic volume growth from this Australian segment. We believe there is plenty more scope for further expansion geographically within Australia. And thirdly, growth through inorganic means or acquisitions. We believe Freightways has delivered well on its acquisitions to date. And given the Australian beach head already in place, we are confident that management can generate further value through additions to the business. Freightways is well positioned to grow in the medium term. Our medium-term thesis still holds despite the short-term blip with the Iran energy situation. Freightways has a very good track record of delivering returns above the cost of capital and a very strong aligned management which makes the business a core holding across several Milford funds.

headline: Devon Funds positive on Freightways as parcel volume growth accelerates to +1.8% and earnings grow 23% in September quarter
reasoning: Freightways operates transport-related businesses across Australasia and serves as a reliable barometer of core NZ business activity, largely disconnected from residential property and major exporters. After two years of declining same-customer parcel volumes, full-year results in August showed minor growth in the first half, and at the AGM in October the company reported same-customer volume growth had accelerated to +1.8% year-on-year in the September quarter. Favourable pricing, cost management and improved network utilisation drove earnings growth of 23% compared to the same quarter last year. Devon holds Freightways as a long-term investment and the stock rallied 7.5% during October, exceeding investor expectations at its AGM.
quote: Freightways operates a range of transport-related businesses across Australasia, but at its core, it's a business-to-business parcel courier company. These parcel volumes are largely disconnected from the residential property market and major exporters like Fonterra and Zespri. Instead, Freightways' courier business serves as a reliable barometer of core NZ business activity. Understandably, their 'same customer' parcel volumes have declined over the past two years. However, their full-year results in August showed minor growth in the first half of the calendar year. At their AGM in late October, the company reported that same customer volume growth had accelerated to +1.8% year on year during the September quarter. Thanks to favourable pricing, sensible cost management, and improved network utilisation, Freightways grew earnings by 23% compared to the same quarter last year - an enviable result for many local companies.
